title: deCH OR Dations
statementMd:
Due to supply chain issues in the North Pole (allegedly caused by a lazy elf), Santa is planning to give out hand-drawn circles as presents this Christmas. Please help him decorate them!

There are $2n$ equally spaced points around the circle, labeled $1,2,\ldots,2n$ in clockwise order. Santa has chosen $n$ chords with **distinct** endpoints, where chord $i$ connects the points $a_i$ and $b_i$. He draws these chords onto the circle one by one, in order.

After Santa has drawn the first $\ell$ chords, consider any non-empty subset $S$ of the $\ell$ chords and let $1\leq c_1 \lt c_2 \lt \cdots \lt c_{|S|}\leq \ell$ be their indices. $S$ is defined to be a *chain* if and only if chord $c_k$ intersects chord $c_{k+1}$ for all $1\leq k \lt |S|$. Note that $S$ is always a *chain* if $|S|=1$.

Santa does not want any chord to be the odd one out. Therefore, he considers the chords to be *tight-knit* if and only if every chord appears in an even number of *chains*, taken over all *chains* that are subsets of the first $\ell$ chords.

For each $\ell$ from $1$ to $n$, help Santa determine whether his chords are *tight-knit*.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2\le n\le 5\cdot 10^5$) — the number of chords.

Then $n$ lines follow, the $i$-th line containing two integers $a_i$ and $b_i$ ($1\le a_i \lt b_i\le 2n$) — the endpoints of the $i$-th chord.

It is guaranteed that all endpoints are distinct.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $5\cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output a string of length $n$ — the $\ell$-th character should be $\texttt{1}$ if the first $\ell$ chords are *tight-knit* and $\texttt{0}$ otherwise.

## Note

In the first test case, no pairs of chords intersect, and thus every chord appears in exactly one *chain* consisting of itself. Therefore, the chords are not *tight-knit* for all $\ell$.

In the second test case, below is an illustration and explanation after the first $\ell=1,2,3,4$ chords are drawn. Sets of chords are denoted as a set of the indices of the corresponding chords.

ExplanationIllustrationChains $\{1\}$. Appearances Chord $1$ appears in $1$ *chain*. Notes The chords are not *tight-knit* since chord $1$ is in an odd number of *chains*. Recall that a set containing a single chord is always a *chain*. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e90e4e43688a02dcde1e51939e07f265cedb2fe9.png)Chains $\{1\}$, $\{1,2\}$, and $\{2\}$. Appearances Chord $1$ appears in $2$ *chains*; Chord $2$ appears in $2$ *chains*. Notes The chords are *tight-knit* since every chord appears in an even number of *chains*. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0aa1fbfb1fc1e791bdeaa1693c386a7b7c96ef82.png)Chains $\{1\}$, $\{1,2\}$, $\{2\}$, and $\{3\}$. Appearances Chord $1$ appears in $2$ *chains*; Chord $2$ appears in $2$ *chains*; Chord $3$ appears in $1$ *chain*. Notes The chords are not *tight-knit* since chord $3$ is in an odd number of *chains*. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/abe547727e598c550451e99aa1af9760320ccb1e.png)Chains $\{1\}$, $\{1,2\}$, $\{1,2,4\}$, $\{2\}$, $\{2,4\}$, $\{3\}$, $\{3,4\}$, and $\{4\}$. Appearances Chord $1$ appears in $3$ *chains*; Chord $2$ appears in $4$ *chains*; Chord $3$ appears in $2$ *chains*; Chord $4$ appears in $4$ *chains*. Notes The chords are not *tight-knit* since chord $1$ is in an odd number of *chains*. Note that $\{2,3,4\}$ is **not** a *chain* since chord $2$ does not intersect chord $3$. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d152e105dc79ce9a3264fb4719fc982b87eb9521.png)

Thus, we output $\mathtt{0100}$.
statementZhMd:
由于北极遭遇供应链问题（据称是一只偷懒的小精灵造成的），圣诞老人打算今年圣诞节送出手绘的圆作为礼物。请帮他装饰这些圆吧！

圆周上有 $2n$ 个等距分布的点，按顺时针顺序依次标号为 $1,2,\ldots,2n$。圣诞老人选定了 $n$ 条端点**互不相同**的弦，其中第 $i$ 条弦连接点 $a_i$ 和 $b_i$。他将这些弦按顺序逐条画到圆上。

在圣诞老人画完前 $\ell$ 条弦后，考虑这 $\ell$ 条弦的任意非空子集 $S$，并设 $1\leq c_1 \lt c_2 \lt \cdots \lt c_{|S|}\leq \ell$ 为 $S$ 中各弦的下标。当且仅当对所有 $1\leq k \lt |S|$，弦 $c_k$ 都与弦 $c_{k+1}$ 相交时，$S$ 才被定义为一个*链*。注意，当 $|S|=1$ 时，$S$ 总是一个*链*。

圣诞老人不希望任何一条弦显得格格不入。因此，当且仅当在所有由前 $\ell$ 条弦的子集构成的*链*中，每条弦出现的次数都是偶数时，他认为这些弦是*紧密相连*的。

对于从 $1$ 到 $n$ 的每个 $\ell$，请帮圣诞老人判断他的弦是否*紧密相连*。

## 输入格式

每个测试文件包含多组测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的组数 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^4$）。接下来是各组测试用例的描述。

每组测试用例的第一行包含一个整数 $n$（$2\le n\le 5\cdot 10^5$）——表示弦的数量。

接下来 $n$ 行，第 $i$ 行包含两个整数 $a_i$ 和 $b_i$（$1\le a_i \lt b_i\le 2n$）——表示第 $i$ 条弦的两个端点。

保证所有端点互不相同。

保证所有测试用例的 $n$ 之和不超过 $5\cdot 10^5$。

## 输出格式

对于每组测试用例，输出一个长度为 $n$ 的字符串——若前 $\ell$ 条弦是*紧密相连*的，则第 $\ell$ 个字符为 $\texttt{1}$，否则为 $\texttt{0}$。

## 说明

在第一组测试用例中，任意两条弦都不相交，因此每条弦恰好只出现在由它自身构成的那一个*链*中。所以对于所有的 $\ell$，这些弦都不是*紧密相连*的。

在第二组测试用例中，下面给出了画出前 $\ell=1,2,3,4$ 条弦之后的图示和解释。弦的集合用相应弦的下标集合表示。

解释 图示 链 $\{1\}$。出现情况 弦 $1$ 出现在 $1$ 条*链*中。备注 这些弦不是*紧密相连*的，因为弦 $1$ 出现在奇数条*链*中。回想一下，只包含单条弦的集合总是一个*链*。![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/e90e4e43688a02dcde1e51939e07f265cedb2fe9.png)链 $\{1\}$、$\{1,2\}$ 和 $\{2\}$。出现情况 弦 $1$ 出现在 $2$ 条*链*中；弦 $2$ 出现在 $2$ 条*链*中。备注 这些弦是*紧密相连*的，因为每条弦都出现在偶数条*链*中。![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0aa1fbfb1fc1e791bdeaa1693c386a7b7c96ef82.png)链 $\{1\}$、$\{1,2\}$、$\{2\}$ 和 $\{3\}$。出现情况 弦 $1$ 出现在 $2$ 条*链*中；弦 $2$ 出现在 $2$ 条*链*中；弦 $3$ 出现在 $1$ 条*链*中。备注 这些弦不是*紧密相连*的，因为弦 $3$ 出现在奇数条*链*中。![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/abe547727e598c550451e99aa1af9760320ccb1e.png)链 $\{1\}$、$\{1,2\}$、$\{1,2,4\}$、$\{2\}$、$\{2,4\}$、$\{3\}$、$\{3,4\}$ 和 $\{4\}$。出现情况 弦 $1$ 出现在 $3$ 条*链*中；弦 $2$ 出现在 $4$ 条*链*中；弦 $3$ 出现在 $2$ 条*链*中；弦 $4$ 出现在 $4$ 条*链*中。备注 这些弦不是*紧密相连*的，因为弦 $1$ 出现在奇数条*链*中。注意，$\{2,3,4\}$ **不是***链*，因为弦 $2$ 与弦 $3$ 不相交。![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d152e105dc79ce9a3264fb4719fc982b87eb9521.png)

因此，我们输出 $\mathtt{0100}$。
